task.prompt:
In Arcady's garden there grows a peculiar apple-tree that fruits one time per year. Its peculiarity can be explained in following way: there are n inflorescences, numbered from 1 to n. Inflorescence number 1 is situated near base of tree and any other inflorescence with number i (i > 1) is situated at the top of branch, which bottom is p_{i}-th inflorescence and p_{i} < i.

Once tree starts fruiting, there appears exactly one apple in each inflorescence. The same moment as apples appear, they start to roll down along branches to the very base of tree. Each second all apples, except ones in first inflorescence simultaneously roll down one branch closer to tree base, e.g. apple in a-th inflorescence gets to p_{a}-th inflorescence. Apples that end up in first inflorescence are gathered by Arcady in exactly the same moment. Second peculiarity of this tree is that once two apples are in same inflorescence they annihilate. This happens with each pair of apples, e.g. if there are 5 apples in same inflorescence in same time, only one will not be annihilated and if there are 8 apples, all apples will be annihilated. Thus, there can be no more than one apple in each inflorescence in each moment of time.

Help Arcady with counting number of apples he will be able to collect from first inflorescence during one harvest.


-----Input-----

First line of input contains single integer number n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100 000)  — number of inflorescences.

Second line of input contains sequence of n - 1 integer numbers p_2, p_3, ..., p_{n} (1 ≤ p_{i} < i), where p_{i} is number of inflorescence into which the apple from i-th inflorescence rolls down.


-----Output-----

Single line of output should contain one integer number: amount of apples that Arcady will be able to collect from first inflorescence during one harvest.


-----Examples-----
Input
3
1 1

Output
1

Input
5
1 2 2 2

Output
3

Input
18
1 1 1 4 4 3 2 2 2 10 8 9 9 9 10 10 4

Output
4



-----Note-----

In first example Arcady will be able to collect only one apple, initially situated in 1st inflorescence. In next second apples from 2nd and 3rd inflorescences will roll down and annihilate, and Arcady won't be able to collect them.

In the second example Arcady will be able to collect 3 apples. First one is one initially situated in first inflorescence. In a second apple from 2nd inflorescence will roll down to 1st (Arcady will collect it) and apples from 3rd, 4th, 5th inflorescences will roll down to 2nd. Two of them will annihilate and one not annihilated will roll down from 2-nd inflorescence to 1st one in the next second and Arcady will collect it.

message.content: {"decision":"HYPOTHESIS_ONLY","suggested_operator_kind":"code_repair","failure_pattern":"Submitted program produces empty output (no value printed) on all audited public cases, yielding WRONG_ANSWER; the source is dominated by an unresolved design deliberation (repeated commented-out reasoning about small-to-large merging and +1 shifting) with no completed merge logic and no final print of the answer.","root_cause_hypothesis":"The generator entered a degenerate self-referential deliberation loop: it repeatedly restated the same small-to-large merge dilemma in comments instead of committing to one correct formulation, so the merge body was never implemented and the required output statement was never emitted. The underlying computational intent (parity/XOR aggregation of shifted child sets up the tree) is plausibly correct, but the code never reaches an executable state.","transferable_operation":"Detect and break deliberation loops in generated code: when the same unresolved sub-decision is restated more than a small number of times without a committed implementation, force a single canonical formulation (here: iterate over the smaller set, toggling t+1 in the larger set, without swapping after shifting), then verify that every required output path emits a value before returning.","expected_benefit":"Converts non-terminating deliberation into a committed, executable merge plus guaranteed output emission, eliminating the empty-output WRONG_ANSWER class and restoring the intended parity-aggregation semantics.","source_evidence_ids":["3d4039df0e43985b4a9b79a1aa61041c89612570595096effc2130b4a5073195"],"applicability_conditions":["Generated code contains repeated near-identical comment blocks restating the same unresolved decision","The program's control flow never reaches a required output/return statement","The intended algorithm is plausibly correct but blocked by an uncommitted sub-step"],"refusal_conditions":["The failure is a genuine algorithmic error rather than an uncommitted deliberation loop","The program already emits output but with wrong values","The repeated comments are intentional documentation, not a loop symptom"],"counterexamples":["A program that deliberates in comments but still emits correct output would not fit this mechanism","A program with a single clear comment and a real logic bug would be misdiagnosed"],"unresolved_uncertainties":["Whether the intended parity/XOR aggregation is itself correct for this task","Whether the empty output is due to missing print versus an exception swallowed by the harness","Whether the deliberation loop is a length-truncation artifact rather than a generation pathology"]}
